senses.definition: The ongoing movement of Earth’s water among air, land, the ground below us, and rivers, lakes, and oceans.
senses.example: When water from a lake becomes part of a cloud, it is moving through the water cycle.

senses.definition: An area of land where streams and runoff all drain toward the same river, lake, or other place.
senses.example: Rain that falls in the watershed runs downhill toward the same creek.

senses.definition: A repeating movement, or a single traveling bump, that carries energy from one place to another.
senses.example: A gust of wind sent waves across the pond.

senses.definition: To move your hand or something you hold back and forth, often to say hello or signal.
senses.example: Please wave so I can spot you in the crowd.

senses.definition: A movement of the hand used as a greeting or signal.
senses.example: Grandpa gave us a wave from the porch.

senses.definition: A path or direction you can take to reach a place.
senses.example: We asked a ranger for the way to the waterfall.

senses.definition: A method of doing something.
senses.example: There is more than one way to solve that puzzle.

senses.definition: To have clothing, jewelry, or something else on your body.
senses.example: I wore a warm hat to watch the game.

senses.definition: To become damaged or worn away little by little from use or rubbing.
senses.example: The stones on the path wore smooth after years of footsteps.

senses.definition: What the air and sky are like in a place at a particular time, including heat, rain, clouds, and wind.
senses.example: The weather was warm before a storm arrived.

senses.definition: To be worn or changed by outdoor conditions, or to get through a hard time.
senses.example: Sun and rain will weather the wooden fence.

senses.definition: To find out how heavy something is, or to be a certain weight.
senses.example: We weighed the package on the kitchen scale.

senses.definition: To think carefully about different choices or facts before deciding.
senses.example: We weighed the good and bad points of taking two different trails.

senses.definition: A word used when showing two or more choices, or when saying that something is uncertain.
senses.example: We did not know whether to take our bikes or walk.

senses.definition: Including all the parts, or still in one piece.
senses.example: The whole class listened to the story.

senses.definition: All of something considered together.
senses.example: The four pieces formed a whole.

senses.definition: To finish in first place or do better than the other side in a contest. It can also mean getting a prize through effort or luck.
senses.example: The green team won its last two games.

senses.definition: The main tube that carries air from your throat toward your lungs.
senses.example: Air moves down your windpipe as you breathe in.

senses.definition: To make letters, words, or symbols so someone can read them later.
senses.example: I wrote her name on the envelope.

senses.definition: To create a story, song, message, or other work by deciding what words or notes go into it.
senses.example: We wrote a play about a lost robot.
